correctness.rationale: Two-branch-point jumps (1,4) follow from Riemann--Hurwitz and Deuring--Shafarevich. Valuation inequalities yield five independent canonical differentials. The Cartier images are explicit, giving ranks 2/3 according to B and stable rank 2. Full automorphisms reduce by the cited unique-index-three-subfield theorem to scaling the base, and the nonzero leading and polar coefficients force the trivial base scaling. Both cases occur over F3; a standalone 36-case checker independently tests the formulas over the prime field, with no inference from finite cases to the general proof.

originality.rationale: A new joint complete stratum classification: both a-number values, exact Cartier coefficient divisor and all full automorphism groups for characteristic-three genus-five, rank-two Artin--Schreier curves. The 2026 paper proves existence only, and the closest older a-number results either have an unmet divisibility hypothesis or yield a nonsharp interval [2,3]. Exact statement, broader implications and nearby database records were compared; implicit classical priority remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older unindexed Cartier-matrix computation for the precise two-pole (4,1) stratum may implicitly cover the divisor; no independence or exhaustive priority claim is made.
The full formal historical literature on Ekedahl--Oort strata was not exhaustively read.

value.rationale: This classifies, rather than samples, the a-number on the natural genus-five, p-rank-two Artin--Schreier stratum. It identifies the exact codimension-one Cartier jump and nilpotent block transition, and establishes that both loci have minimal full automorphism group. This directly informs the motivating 2026 question about simultaneous control of symmetry, p-rank and a-number; coefficient-normalization/negative checks alone would not give the asserted classification.
